cards.title: RBI Circular (31 Dec 2019): Comprehensive Cyber Security Framework for Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks - A Graded Approach (Regulator's Document)
cards.key_problem: The Reserve Bank of India's own circular requiring urban co-operative banks to self-assess into four levels by digital depth and payment-system interconnection and implement progressively stronger cyber-security controls.
key_outcomes: RBI/2019-20/129, DoS.CO/CSITE/BC.4083/31.01.052/2019-20, dated 31 December 2019, signed by R. Ravikumar, CGM, Department of Supervision

Four levels: Level I all UCBs; Level II sub-members of CPS offering internet/mobile banking or direct CTS/IMPS/UPI members; Level III direct CPS members or those with own ATM switch or SWIFT; Level IV own ATM switch and SWIFT, or hosting a data centre for other banks
Level I (Annex I): bank-specific email domain with DMARC, dynamic two-factor authentication for CBS and CBS-connected apps, password policy, vendor/outsourcing risk management

Level II: data-loss-prevention strategy, anti-phishing, VA/PT of critical apps; Level III: disable remote connections and RDP to RTGS/NEFT/ATM switch/SWIFT systems, centralised IAM with MFA, advanced threat defence; Level IV: C-SOC and IT/IS governance
Self-assessment to the RBI regional office within 45 days; Level I controls within 3 months

cards.title: Work from Home for BPO / KPO and Contact-Centre Agents (2020): VDI for CRM plus Turbo UDP Tunnel for VoIP, with a Bank Contact-Centre Case
cards.client: An Indian bank with five contact centres on an Android VoIP app, moving about 500 agents to work from home
cards.key_problem: Contact-centre and back-office agents working from home need CRM apps without installing them on personal PCs, GSM-quality VoIP over home internet, data protection, productivity audit and a fixed IP per agent to meet DoT rules.
key_outcomes: Architecture: contact-centre apps delivered on virtual desktops, the VoIP softphone runs locally and reaches the voice system (Avaya, Aspect, Cisco, Genesys) through the access gateway
Accops Turbo UDP tunnel (Noise, Curve25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305): 1,011 Mbps vs 825-881 Mbps IPsec and 258 Mbps OpenVPN; 0.403 ms ping vs 0.52 ms and 1.54 ms
Unique static virtual IP per agent at every login to satisfy DoT regulations; device binding, geolocation, host checks, copy/print/screen-record blocking, internet blocking, productivity reports
Comparison table vs other VPNs and other VDI on 14 needs (VoIP performance, credential and device sharing, fixed IP, watermarking)
Case: a bank's ~500 agents on an Android VoIP app brought online from home; agents cannot log in from multiple devices
Licensing: subscription or perpetual, named or concurrent, 24x7 support
cards.brief: A 2020 pandemic-era slide deck for BPO, KPO and contact-centre operators. It lists the business need for home working and its risks, the needs of the organisation and the agent, and an architecture that separates app delivery (virtual desktops) from voice (local softphone through the HySecure Turbo tunnel). It explains Turbo's cryptography and fixed virtual IP, shows throughput and latency against IPsec and OpenVPN, lists Digital Workspace controls, compares Accops with generic VPNs and VDI, walks through a bank contact-centre case, and ends with licensing, a 2020 company profile, customer lists and a Nano secure-USB slide.
cards.use_for: A BPO, KPO, contact centre or bank call-centre prospect asking how agents can work from home with softphones, a fixed IP for DoT compliance and no data on the home PC. Also the clearest short explanation of the Turbo VoIP tunnel.
cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2020, pandemic framing; company figures (500+ customers, 100+ team, 400,000 users) are years out of date. Refers to 'Accops DPAN technology' once, apparently a legacy name for Turbo. DoT OSP rules for WFH were relaxed in 2020-21 - check whether the static-IP requirement still applies.
cards.internal_reason: Marked 'Accops Confidential'; no verified public URL.
cards.needs_human: A .pptx twin exists in the same folder (clears by stem). The BPO case study (Dataquest / FiveS-style stories) in the paid-media folder may be a better current proof point.

cards.title: Zero Trust Computing for Defence Services (March 2022): Internet Isolation, Virtual Browser with CDR, Nano Secure USB and Multi-Layer Gateway Architecture
cards.client: Indian defence, government and PSU customers: a defence staff HQ, the Air Force, a defence research lab, the national informatics centre, a nuclear power utility, an atomic research centre, an insurer, oil and steel PSUs, the tax board, a bank and a depository; international government customers in Japan, UAE and Oman
cards.client_actual: HQ IDS (100), Airforce (5,000+), DRDO Delhi (100+), NIC (1 lakh+), NPCIL (1,200), IGCAR Kalpakkam (1,000), NTPC/SAIL, LIC (500), HPCL, CBDT (1,000), Canara Bank SWIFT (300), CDSL, MDL; Ibaraki Prefecture, Dubai Courts, Abu Dhabi Development Fund, RCA Oman
cards.key_problem: Defence and critical organisations rely on vLAN and IP-based segmentation, dual PCs for internet access and L3 VPNs, which expose networks to user devices, leak data and cost money, while internet browsing brings malware, APTs and supply-chain attacks inside.
key_outcomes: Defence/government/PSU reference table with use case and users: e.g. Air Force training labs and VDI 5,000+, NIC web VPN and secure browser 1 lakh+, IGCAR virtual work PCs for 1,000 scientists, NPCIL secure browser 1,200, Canara Bank SWIFT security 300
Zero-trust access model and ZTNA gateway that hides application servers; VDI as software-defined isolation with security, productivity, compliance and cost benefits

Safe internet surfing: dual thick PCs vs virtual browser (three designs, incl. a defence internet cloud), session/host/file security, CDR and AV scanning for downloads; case slides for a defence lab, an atomic research centre and a 25,000-user Japanese prefecture

Remote access design for critical apps: Nano bootable USB with fingerprint and FIDO2, HySecure Turbo (WireGuard-based, Curve25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305) on UDP 443, HyLite HTML5 gateway, HyWorks VDI; protocols and ports; FIPS-compliant set-up; Reporting Server logging
Multi-layered gateway option: an outer VPN from a different vendor with PKI plus an inner ZTNA gateway with MFA and continuous face monitoring, traffic through WAF
2022 company snapshot: 600+ customers, 250+ partners, 150+ team, 600,000+ users; Class I Make-in-India OEM; first cyber-security provider on GeM; NASSCOM Emerge 50 2020
cards.brief: A 90-slide March 2022 deck ('Last modified 16 March 2022') presented by the CTO to defence services. After company, founder and recognition slides and a defence / government / PSU customer table, it is organised around four themes: zero-trust network access (why vLAN/IP segmentation fails), virtual computing (VDI as a software air gap, use cases by security, mobility, cost and compliance), virtualising the internet (virtual browser designs, security of channel, session, host and downloads, CDR, case slides), and secure remote access over the internet (Nano secure USB logon process, Turbo and HyLite security analysis, VPN vs ZTNA vs VDI options, multi-layer gateway). It closes with the product portfolio.
cards.use_for: Defence, paramilitary, PSU, nuclear/atomic, research or any air-gapped government prospect: internet isolation instead of dual PCs, secure remote access to classified or critical apps, and a defence-in-depth architecture with ports and protocols for a technical committee.
cards.stale_risk: March 2022; company figures (600+ customers, 150+ team) are out of date and the deck predates the Reliance acquisition. Breach statistics cited are IBM 2019. Customer/user counts are as of 2022. The newer 'Accops Defence Brochure Nov 25 V4' (carded earlier) is the current customer-facing piece.

cards.needs_human: Confirm the defence and government customers (HQ IDS, DRDO, Airforce, IGCAR, NPCIL) may be named even to other government prospects.
